findings.finding: The first formal FY27 guide lands in this release. In August management gave only direction: reported revenue +0-1% (3% NASA insourcing headwind and 1% base-ops exit, more than offset by mid-single-digit growth elsewhere), adjusted EBITDA margin up about 20bp, and 'continued strong EPS and FCF growth' from lower interest and integration costs, with about 92% of FY27 revenue from existing or follow-on work. If 'strong EPS growth' means high single digits on a FY26 base of about $2.45, the guide clears an implied forward EPS of about $2.53 (forward P/E 8.25, single aggregator).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Nov 2025 the FY26 guide in the Q4 release was followed by +18.25%. In Aug 2026 an EPS raise plus a revenue cut and the preliminary FY27 revenue of 0-1% was followed by -8.22%. The guide line moves this stock both ways in size.
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side cut targets on the revenue framework (BTIG 9x EV/EBITDA, MS $24, GS $24, RBC $25), and the stock trades at about 8.3x forward EPS with a put skew. If the market had priced the EPS and FCF growth management described, the multiple would not sit at a 44% drawdown with puts bid. The weakness is that the FY27 EPS consensus is not sourced, so the size of the gap is unknown.
findings.independence: Same management statement as the August revenue framework (https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/btig-cuts-amentum-stock-price-target-on-muted-2027-outlook-93CH-4854372). The deleveraging that drives the EPS growth is in the 8-K: net leverage 3.0x and a $125M voluntary term-loan prepayment (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002011286/000162828026055294/exhibit991-august102026.htm).

findings.finding: Q4 revenue consensus of about $3.70B sits about 0.8% above the guide-implied midpoint of $3.67B (range $3.595-3.745B, from FY26 revenue guidance of $13.80-13.95B less $10,205M year to date). The guide was just cut for $175M of protest-delayed new business and lower materials volume, so the consensus needs the upper half of a freshly lowered range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Aug 2026: revenue below the $3.60B consensus and a revenue-guide cut sold -8.22% despite an EPS beat and raise. Feb 2026: -12.38% on a shutdown-hit Q1.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews report a flat EPS consensus over 60 days and $3.70B revenue, so the street has not moved toward the guide midpoint. A priced risk would show a consensus at or below $3.67B. The gap is inside the company's own guide, so the market was told to expect a range that includes a small miss, which is why the finding is small.
findings.independence: Consensus sources: Investing.com preview 2026-11-20 (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/amentum-earnings-loom-ahead-as-eps-forecast-signals-decline-93CH-5042051) and MarketBeat/Longbridge snippets. Management said about 99% of Q4 revenue is follow-on work and the midpoint implies about 2% normalized growth (Fool transcript), which argues for landing near the midpoint rather than the top.

findings.finding: This season the govcon tape has sold revenue-light prints even with EPS beats and raised EPS guides: Leidos -6.55% (Q3 revenue $4.63B vs $4.714B, full-year revenue guide lowered, EPS guide raised; 2026-11-03), Parsons -6.9% (weak full-year revenue guide; 2026-10-28), KBR -5.5% (Mission Tech revenue -5% on NASA reductions, guide reaffirmed; 2026-10-29). Amentum's own Q3 followed the same pattern at -8.22%. A flat FY27 revenue guide is the likely headline here.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: AMTM Aug 2026: EPS $0.67 vs $0.61 consensus with the EPS guide raised, revenue cut, stock -8.22%. The name has not paid for EPS raises when revenue is weak.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the +6.48 put skew and the fade from $23.13 to $20.9 since 2026-11-10 lean the same way. What is less visible is that a FY27 revenue guide of about 0-1% was pre-announced in August, so the 'flat revenue' headline may already be in the price. Either way, the peer pattern says EPS strength will not be rewarded without revenue.
findings.independence: Parsons: https://www.webull.com/news/15825822278968320 (2026-10-28). KBR: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/earnings-kbr-nyse-kbr-announces-earnings-results-2026-10-29/. Counter-evidence: V2X raised revenue guidance (https://www.morningstar.com/news/pr-newswire/20261102la86728/v2x-reports-third-quarter-2026-results) and CACI raised with 2.0x book-to-bill (https://www.govconwire.com/articles/caci-q1-fy27-revenues-contract-awards-outlook). This finding is a peer proxy.

findings.finding: Award flow since the Q3 call supports Q4 bookings and FY27 visibility. In August, COSMOS (~$500M) and Langley CMOE II ($974M) cleared protest. Since then: Cheyenne Mountain NISSC III $572.4M (2026-09-28), Sellafield JV preferred supplier up to £2.1B (2026-09-30), NASA $256M (Oct 7), Navy multi-engine training $490M (Oct 28), Army $609M through 2031 (Nov 5). That is against a backlog of $48.2B and a Q3 book-to-bill of 1.1x, with about $2B of won-but-protested work.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The $974M NASA Langley win moved the stock +3% on its day (https://finviz.com/news/384229/amentum-shares-rise-3-after-securing-974-million-nasa-contract). Bookings did not offset the revenue cut in August.
findings.why_not_priced: Each award was press-released, so individually they are priced. What the market cannot see yet is the Q4 book-to-bill and how much of the ~$2B protested work converted. A low book-to-bill would be visible as a further de-rating, and a strong one is what a flat-revenue FY27 needs to read as temporary.
findings.independence: Sellafield: https://www.niauk.org/amentum-joint-venture-secures-preferred-position-for-major-uk-nuclear-contract/. $609M Army: Investing.com preview 2026-11-20 (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/amentum-earnings-loom-ahead-as-eps-forecast-signals-decline-93CH-5042051). Peer demand: Parsons Federal awards +53% YoY (https://www.govconwire.com/articles/parsons-q3-2026-federal-solutions-awards-carey-smith).

findings.finding: NASA insourcing is proceeding as guided, not worse. Amentum filed a WARN notice for 70 jobs at Kennedy Space Center (effective by 2026-11-30) as NASA takes base operations in house, and KBR's Mission Tech revenue fell 5% on 'anticipated' NASA reductions. Both are consistent with the 3% FY27 headwind management already guided, at the 'upper bound' of its scenarios.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The NASA headwind going from 1% to 3% in August was part of the -8.22% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced because it was guided. The residual risk is that the 3% grows again, given NASA's broader plan (a single secondary source cites 7,500 contractor positions). If that were priced, the FY27 revenue bar would already sit below 0%.
findings.independence: KBR Q3 FY26: https://chemxplore.com/news/kbr-third-quarter-fiscal-2026-results. Amentum KSC layoffs: https://layoffhedge.com/company/amentum (tracker, secondary).

findings.finding: There was no shutdown in Q1 FY27. A CR funds the government from 2026-10-01 to 2026-12-11 (CRS R49353), while Q1 FY26 was hit by the fall-2025 shutdown, so the FY27 Q1 comparison is easy. Management's base case already assumed a CR through most of Q1. There is about 20% shutdown risk at the Dec 11 deadline (Statt), which management may cite to keep the guide cautious.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026: -12.38% on the shutdown-hit Q1 FY26.
findings.why_not_priced: Public macro and consistent with the company's assumption, so it is largely priced. It is filed because it removes a downside scenario for Q1 commentary. Macro-to-company proxy.
findings.independence: https://statt.com/blog/december-11-government-shutdown-deadline-whats-next-for-fy2027-funding/ ; management's CR assumption in the Fool transcript.

findings.finding: Q4 needs about $312-362M of free cash flow to hit the unchanged FY26 FCF guide of $525-575M (year to date $213M, per the 8-K cash-flow statement). Management cited seasonally strong collections and one fewer pay cycle, and said it was 'on track' for net leverage below 3x in Q4. Buybacks are on the capital-allocation list, and the stock trades at about 8x forward EPS. A sub-3x print could bring a first repurchase authorization.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior buyback announcement exists to compare against. Deleveraging milestones did not offset the revenue reaction in August.
findings.why_not_priced: No authorization has been filed (EDGAR shows no 8-K since 2026-10-02 other than the executive chair's agreement). A priced buyback would need an announced program. A large Q4 back-end FCF is also a risk if collections slip, so the range is two-sided.
findings.independence: Shares the 8-K with finding 2. The management commentary on buybacks and leverage is in the Fool transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/19/amentum-amtm-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/).

findings.finding: Short interest rose to 14.05M shares (9.23% of float, 7.2-7.55 days to cover) at the Oct 30 settlement from 12.33M, and the stock faded 10% from its Nov 10 high into the print, with a +6.48 put skew. Bears are positioned for a revenue disappointment, so an acceptable FY27 guide meets a short base that takes 7+ days to cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 2025: +18.25% on the Q4/FY guide print, the largest reaction in the history.
findings.why_not_priced: The short base and the skew are themselves the market's price of the downside. The asymmetry is that a squeeze mechanism exists only on the upside. Not crowded enough (under 10% of float) to be large.
findings.independence: https://massive.com/quote/amtm (14.05M, 7.2 days, as of 2026-10-30); price path https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/amtm/history/.

lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar): the FY27 EPS consensus is unsourced (one aggregator forward P/E), so the FY27 guidance finding is capped from +1.5 to +0.8.
Rule 6 / core (inside guide): the Q4 revenue gap sits inside the company's guided range, so it goes from -0.8 toward 0, to -0.5. NASA insourcing is inside the guided 3%, so -0.3 becomes -0.2.
Rules 5 and 7: the peer revenue-reaction finding is a proxy that agrees with the put skew, and short interest is 9.2% of float with 7.5 days to cover, so it goes from -1.5 to -0.9.
Rule 5: the awards are public press releases (partly priced), so +1.0 becomes +0.6. The buyback/FCF item is an inference, so +0.5 becomes +0.3. Positioning goes from +0.5 to +0.4.
